faqs.question: What are LIPEX liposome extruders used for?
faqs.answer: LIPEX extruders are used to produce uniform, size-controlled liposomes and lipid nanoparticles by forcing lipid suspensions through defined-pore filters, widely used across liposomal drug product manufacturing.

faqs.question: What pressure range does LIPEX operate at?
faqs.answer: Standard LIPEX extruders operate at 100 to 2400 psi, while the newer LIPEX Flow reaches up to 2450 psi (170 bar).

faqs.question: What is LIPEX Flow, and how is it different?
faqs.answer: LIPEX Flow is the newly designed extruder incorporating a novel drain cavity, reducing extrusion pressure by over 50% while increasing maximum operating pressure, resulting in higher throughput and faster batch processing.

faqs.question: What batch volumes can LIPEX extruders handle?
faqs.answer: LIPEX extruders scale from 1 mL at the laboratory benchtop to hundreds of liters at commercial scale, with 10 mL, 100 mL, and 1000 mL standard units covering different development stages.

faqs.question: What is LIPEX made from?
faqs.answer: LIPEX extruders are manufactured from durable, high-quality 316L stainless steel, with no moving parts.

faqs.question: Can LIPEX Flow handle difficult-to-extrude formulations?
faqs.answer: Yes, its higher operating pressure of up to 2450 psi benefits formulations like hydrophobics or concentrated lipid suspensions that are harder to extrude.

faqs.question: Does LIPEX Flow reduce filter clogging?
faqs.answer: Yes, the combination of reduced extrusion pressure and increased operating pressure allows more material to be extruded with reduced filter clogging and less frequent filter changes.

faqs.question: Is LIPEX suitable for GMP commercial production?
faqs.answer: Yes, 142mm and 293mm stand-alone filter holders integrate into turnkey, automated skid systems for large-scale GMP production.

longForm.heroHook: Nearly 30 years setting the industry standard for liposomal drug product manufacturing.
longForm.heroLead: Achieving a specified vesicle size reproducibly, batch after batch, is what separates a viable liposomal drug product from an inconsistent one. LIPEX has been the industry's answer to that problem for decades. Built from durable, high-quality 316L stainless steel with no moving parts, LIPEX liposome extruders force aqueous lipid suspensions through polycarbonate filters at pressures between 100 and 2400 psi, converting heterogeneous multi-lamellar vesicles into a homogeneous population of large unilamellar vesicles. The newly designed LIPEX Flow pushes that further, with a novel drain cavity, over 50% reduced extrusion pressure, and operating pressure up to 2450 psi, supporting higher throughput and faster batch processing without sacrificing particle quality.

sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: LIPEX liposome extruders product information: extrusion mechanics, scale-up range, and LIPEX Flow improvements.
body: LIPEX extruders use a one-step process, forcing aqueous lipid suspensions through filters of a defined pore size to produce a homogeneous population of large unilamellar vesicles from a heterogeneous multi-lamellar starting suspension.

Pressures of 100 to 2400 psi force vesicles through polycarbonate filters, with relatively gentle pressure and controlled temperature ensuring optimal particle size reduction, a homogeneous population, and high yield.
Construction uses durable, high-quality 316L stainless steel, with no moving parts, keeping maintenance requirements minimal even under consistent production use.
LIPEX Flow, the newly designed model, incorporates a novel drain cavity that increases throughput capacity without affecting the ability to reduce particle size.
Extrusion pressure drops by more than 50% on LIPEX Flow, ensuring higher flow rates at lower pressures, while maximum operating pressure increases to 2450 psi (170 bar) for formulations that need it.
That combination allows more material to be extruded with reduced filter clogging and less frequent filter changes, leading to faster batch processing without compromising particle quality.
The new design also minimizes process risk by reducing the need to open extruders, lowering contamination or safety exposure when handling HPAPIs.
Difficult-to-extrude formulations, including hydrophobics or concentrated lipid suspensions, benefit directly from the higher operating pressure LIPEX Flow makes available.

sections.title: Gentle Pressure, Uniform Particles
sections.description: Some particle-sizing technologies achieve uniform vesicles by pushing formulations hard. LIPEX takes the opposite approach, using relatively gentle pressure at controlled temperature instead. That gentler process is what ensures optimal particle size reduction alongside a homogeneous population and high yield, rather than trading one of those outcomes off against another. The one-step extrusion process itself, forcing aqueous lipid suspensions through filters of a defined pore size, converts a heterogeneous starting population of multi-lamellar vesicles directly into uniform large unilamellar vesicles. With LIPEX Flow's novel drain cavity design, that same gentle-pressure principle now runs at higher throughput, since the pressure reduction of over 50% means more material moves through the system without pushing particle formation harder than necessary.

sections.eyebrow: Scaling from Lab to Commercial Production
sections.title: Scaling from Lab to Commercial Production
sections.description: How LIPEX extruders match batch volume to process stage, from 1 mL to commercial-scale production.
body: A liposomal formulation that works at 10 mL doesn't automatically translate to a 1000-liter batch, and matching extruder scale to process stage is what keeps that translation reliable.

During initial R&D and pre-clinical work, 10 mL benchtop units support formulation feasibility and small-scale development directly. Moving into early-stage clinical trials, 100 mL and 1000 mL units enable rapid scale-up without a full process redesign. For large-scale GMP production supporting late-stage clinical trials or commercial batches, 142mm and 293mm stand-alone filter holders integrate into turnkey, automated skid systems using both nitrogen pressure and pharmaceutical-grade pumps. Standard sizes cover most process requirements, and customized, purpose-built equipment is available where a process calls for something tailored specifically to it.
